note: The textbook case and the only one in this batch. He bought a 48-year-old business seven years ago and overhauled it, after thirteen years flying helicopters professionally — squarely 'business owner or equivalent'. Income is confirmed by the buyer himself in the plainest terms available: 'I can afford it, but it's not about that.' Health is the neglected area rather than a crisis — no conditions, testosterone in range, ten thousand steps every morning, a gym membership and a home gym — and he wants lean flexibility and vitality into his older years rather than rescue. He is nowhere near the deconditioned gym-averse exclusion. The only wobble is good_to_great, which he demurred on himself when the rep described the client base — 'I'm probably not good yet, but... I look fine with my shirt off, and I feel good, but I have a lot of endurance and strength to rebuild up' — but 27% DEXA body fat targeting 15%, with a history of reaching 12-13%, is a good-to-great arc rather than a rescue. Scored core. The finding this produces is the important one for the rollup: across this batch the two deals that closed were both outside the stated ICP on three criteria each, and the single core-ICP prospect left asking for testimonials. On this call the rep also stated the ICP live and quantitatively — 'The people who get our program are mostly people who are good looking to go to great', '70% of the people I speak to are business owners', 'I'd say 40% of the people I speak to already have abs', 'We don't have those people' — which his own pipeline in this same folder does not support.
